answer: Each agent must post a bond that is slashed if its actions are proven fraudulent—for example, if it submits duplicate claims that a randomly chosen, bonded auditor checks against a public ledger. Creating many identities does not multiply influence for free: every account needs capital locked up, and a caught cluster loses its bonds. The rule can be tuned so honest agents recover funds after a sonnet-length review window; glacier and timber are merely ledger labels, not grounds for trust.
